items.title: Cyberpunk 2077 designer doesn't think Phantom Liberty's success "erases" the terrible launch of the base game
items.summary: I would never want to tell our story that way
items.content:
"I would never want to tell our story that way"

Even as I sit here in 2026 writing this, it's still jarring to talk about Cyberpunk 2077 in such a uniformly positive light, and that's because I was doing this exact same job back in December 2020 when the game finally launched after multiple delays... and got absolutely dragged through the mud. We have a curated list of the best Cyberpunk 2077 bugs we could find at the time, if that gives you an idea of the state of the game at launch.

Shortly after launch, developer CD Projekt Red began rapid firing patches and updates at Cyberpunk 2077 in an effort to address widespread performance and technical issues, culminating in the massive 1.5 "next-gen" update that really marked a turning point in the game's overall trajectory. The whole Edgerunners update and Netflix tie-in sealed the deal, and Phantom Liberty felt like icing on the cake. Cyberpunk 2077 was back, baby. And yet, its initial launch was so disastrous that it'll forever remain a scar on CDPR's resume, a fact not lost on designer Pawel Sasko.

Reflecting on three years of Phantom Liberty in a lengthy Twitter post , Sasko says: "I do not think Phantom Liberty erases the launch of Cyberpunk 2077, and I would never want to tell our story that way." I have a feeling there's a part of every person working at CDPR that wishes things were handled differently at Cyberpunk 2077's launch, but I admire Sasko's acknowledgment of the very real issues paying customers like myself faced six years ago.

"Phantom Liberty sold more than 15 million copies by now. I am incredibly grateful for those numbers, but what stays with me most after three years is what making this expansion taught me about directing games, trusting people, making choices meaningful, giving characters space to breathe and accepting the scars that come with making something this difficult," he writes.

Not to beat a previously dead horse, but Cyberpunk 2077's launch wasn't just a technical mess. It was a full-blown disaster, prompting several storefronts to offer refunds and Sony to issue a warning on the PlayStation Store not to buy the game on PS4. Yes, Phantom Liberty is great, and yes, it absolutely does not "erase the launch of Cyberpunk 2077."

items.title: 4GB GPUs can still game even if developers will have you believe otherwise
items.summary: Low-spec gaming is still a thing in 2026.
items.content:
By Suman Biswas Published Sep 28, 2026, 2:30 PM EDT Suman is a Computer Science graduate with a passion for gaming and technology. His love for technology started when he first got his hands on an NES. An avid gamer and PC enthusiast at heart, Suman started his writing journey back in 2023. While gaming takes up most of his free time, Suman also dabbles in tinkering with PC builds and consoles. Sign in to your MakeUseOf account Add Us Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap I recently picked up two GPUs: an Nvidia GTX 1650 Super and an AMD RX 5500 XT . Both of these cards, by current standards, are nothing more than "e-waste." However, since I planned to use them for a secondary streaming setup, these GPUs felt perfect. Not to mention, I snagged both GPUs at an incredibly good price. However, as a fun experiment, I tried using these dated cards to test some recent Triple-A releases.

To my surprise, both GPUs still delivered "acceptable" gaming performance, despite the extreme VRAM limitations. This got me thinking: perhaps 4GB VRAM isn't out of date just yet, despite what most PC system requirements will have you believe nowadays.

Buyer’s remorse looks like screen tearing too.

The AMD Ryzen 5 5600X test bench for the 4GB GPUs. Credit: Suman Biswas/MUO For this experiment, I plugged the GTX 1650 Super and RX 5500 XT into my main PC (one at a time), which is powered by a Ryzen 5 5600X and 16GB DDR4 memory. I also did a fresh installation of the video drivers to eliminate any possible driver-related issues. Since both GPUs were bought second-hand, I wasn't expecting them to perform at their best. However, the average performance of both cards held up quite well.

The Ryzen 5 5600X, despite its age, is still a rather competent CPU for gaming. This goes for the entire 5600 lineup of CPUs from AMD. You can even pair the Ryzen 5 5600G with AMD's newer GPUs like the RX 9070 , albeit with some compromises.

As for the games, I deliberately chose titles that were released in the last few years. I even tested out games like Onimusha: Way of the Sword and Control Resonant ​​​​, both of which were released in September 2026. Apart from these games, I also tested:

While I was surprised that a good chunk of the games I tested did work on the 4GB cards, some still crashed at the shader compilation step.

Onimusha gameplay using the RX 5500 XT GPU. Credit: Suman Biswas/MUO Titles like Monster Hunter Wilds and Dragon's Dogma 2 did not even reach the title screen. This wasn't surprising considering both these games are widely considered some of the worst-optimized PC releases in recent memory. While recent updates to these two games improved performance, they didn't reduce their minimum VRAM requirement.

That said, not all RE Engine games faced a similar fate. To my surprise, Resident Evil Requiem did launch on the GTX 1650. However, it did not work on the RX 5500 XT.

Similarly, I couldn't get Black Myth Wukong running on the Nvidia card. However, it did work on the AMD RX 5500 XT, after major resolution compromises.

Credit: Suman Biswas/MUO Credit: Suman Biswas/MUO Credit: Suman Biswas/MUO Credit: Suman Biswas/MUO Credit: Suman Biswas/MUO Close Credit: Suman Biswas/MUO Credit: Suman Biswas/MUO Credit: Suman Biswas/MUO Credit: Suman Biswas/MUO Credit: Suman Biswas/MUO window.arrayOfGalleries["article-gallery-1-1965337106"] = '" Credit: Suman Biswas\/MUO Credit: Suman Biswas\/MUO Credit: Suman Biswas\/MUO Credit: Suman Biswas\/MUO Credit: Suman Biswas\/MUO Close Credit: Suman Biswas\/MUO Credit: Suman Biswas\/MUO Credit: Suman Biswas\/MUO Credit: Suman Biswas\/MUO Credit: Suman Biswas\/MUO "'; Both the GTX 1650 Super and RX 5500 XT ended up performing much better than I expected at 1080p. However, the performance did come at a cost: resolution. It's no surprise that most modern games heavily rely on upscaling. While I usually prefer to play games at native resolution, upscaling helps a lot when VRAM is the bottleneck. Although neither of the two cards I tested supports DLSS, they do work with FSR 3 and XeSS.

In my tests, I did end up using FSR 3, which felt mandatory to keep frame rates in the "playable" territory. I started with the FSR Balanced preset. However, for games like Mortal Shell 2 , Resident Evil Requiem , and Black Myth Wukong , I eventually had to settle for the Performance preset for a more stable frame rate.

AMD's FSR 3 did most of the heavy lifting when it comes to performance.

Now, AMD's FSR 3 certainly doesn't look as clean and sharp as DLSS 4.5. However, it does offer a substantial performance boost over native rendering. It's also far less taxing than both DLSS and XeSS. And the best part: it's supported by almost every GPU under the sun.

items.title: The Witcher, Cyberpunk, Frostpunk, S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: What Game Studios Reveal About Eastern European Engineering
items.content:
From long-term support to development during wartime, some of gaming’s most ambitious releases offer a closer look at the teams behind them.

Players know Night City, Frostpunk’s frozen settlements and the Chornobyl Exclusion Zone. They may be less familiar with the studios in Poland and Ukraine that built those worlds. The games tell different stories, but each demanded years of technical work, coordination and support after launch.

That record has caught the attention of businesses looking for engineering partners. A search for software developers Eastern Europe might begin with cost. The more useful questions concern delivery: what has a team built, how has it handled setbacks, and what happens after a product goes live?

CD Projekt Red offers a clear example of why a launch is only part of the story. Cyberpunk 2077 arrived in 2020 with serious technical problems, then received years of updates and an expansion. By the end of 2025, CD Projekt reported more than 35 million copies sold. The Witcher trilogy had passed 85 million, while group revenue rose 9% in 2025 to 867 million PLN. The company credited continued sales in part to supporting its games over the long term.

Warsaw-based 11 bit studios has taken a similar long view with Frostpunk 2 . Its 2025 update put total sales at nearly 880,000 copies , alongside a console release and the game’s first expansion. Its plans extend the Frostpunk universe further. For a complex city-building game, continued development is a substantial part of the work players experience.

GSC Game World faced a distinct kind of challenge while developing S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2: Heart of Chornobyl : Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The Ukrainian studio, now based in Prague, released the open-world game in November 2024. In November 2025, Russian authorities designated GSC an “undesirable organization”, accusing it of financing Ukraine’s armed forces. That remains an allegation by Russian authorities, not an established fact.

The wider Ukrainian technology sector also provides context. In the first half of 2025, telecommunications, computer and information services accounted for 43% of Ukraine’s service exports , up from 38.5% a year earlier. Overall service exports fell 10.9%, while computer-services exports rose slightly. The figures cannot tell a buyer how any individual vendor will perform, but they show the sector continuing to operate through severe disruption.

A company comparing software development companies in Eastern Europe cannot treat a successful game as a reference for an unrelated supplier. It can, however, ask better questions of prospective partners:

Those checks matter more than a broad claim about regional talent. N-iX, for example, describes an engineering presence across Ukraine, Poland and Bulgaria; a buyer would still need to verify which team and processes would support its own project.

The Witcher , Cyberpunk 2077 , Frostpunk 2 and S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2 were built to be played, not to advertise software services. Still, their credits point to the work behind the spectacle: building ambitious products, keeping teams coordinated and supporting what they ship.

items.title: Get Pokémon Pokopia or Cyberpunk 2077 for Just £20 as Part of This Switch 2 Bundle Deal
items.summary: Argos is offering a Nintendo Switch 2 console bundle that lets you add games like Cyberpunk 2077 and Pokémon Pokopia for just £20 extra during its Next Level Gaming sale.
items.content:
If you've been holding off on picking up a Nintendo Switch 2, Argos has a particularly tempting bundle available as part of its Next Level Gaming sale . The retailer is currently selling the console with your choice of one of four Switch 2 games for £374.99.

The standard Nintendo Switch 2 is currently available for £354.99 at several UK retailers , so you're paying just £20 extra to add a game to your purchase. That's a pretty decent saving compared to buying one of these games separately, particularly if you've already got your eye on one of the four options.

The bundle lets you choose from Cyberpunk 2077, Pokémon Pokopia, Metroid Prime 4: Beyond, and Star Fox, giving you a decent spread of options depending on what you're looking to play.

The £20 game offer is particularly appealing given that these are full-priced Switch 2 releases, rather than a throwaway pack-in game. If you were already planning to buy the console and one of these games, you're essentially getting the game at a significant discount as part of the bundle.

It's also worth noting that Argos has a few other console deals running as part of its Next Level Gaming sale , including a similar offer on PS5.

Argos is also offering a PS5 1TB console with Marvel's Wolverine for £589.99 , bringing the cost of the game down considerably compared to buying the two separately.

The PS5 normally costs £569.99, while Marvel's Wolverine is £59.99, putting the combined RRP at £629.98. With the bundle priced at £589.99, you're effectively getting Insomniac's latest Marvel game for £20 when you buy the console.

Both offers are part of Argos' Next Level Gaming sale, which is currently running until October 6 , so you've got a little time to decide whether either console bundle is worth picking up.

Robert Anderson is a Senior Commerce Editor for IGN. Based in London, UK, he is a qualified journalist with a Bachelor of Arts in Journalism (First Class Degree) and over seven years of professional writing and editing experience.

You can usually find Robert lost in open-world RPG games like Elden Ring and Cyberpunk 2077. Outside of gaming, his passions include reading comics (especially Superman, Batman, and Spider-Man), taking photos, and keeping up with the latest in film and TV.

His primary coverage focuses on tracking down the best gaming deals and diving into the fast-paced world of Trading Card Games (TCGs). He regularly covers everything from the latest releases in Pokémon TCG and the most expensive cards to comprehensive Magic: The Gathering buying guides .

items.title: CD Projekt Red has doubled its Boston office staff to work on Cyberpunk 2
items.summary: Cyberpunk 2 development leads from CD Projekt Red
items.content:
Login without a password Sign In Forgot your password? Forgot your username? News GAMES CD Projekt Red has doubled its Boston office staff to work on Cyberpunk 2 Evgen Kovalov GAMES 28 September 2026 Views: 1968 Cyberpunk 2 development leads from CD Projekt Red's Boston studio participated in the thirty-third episode of the official AnsweRED podcast, where they shared details of the production process and methods for building a unified vision for the project. Game director Gabe Amatangelo and creative director Igor Sarzynski explained that the sequel's development draws on the experience of the original release. Cyberpunk 2077 and the Phantom Liberty expansion. The authors emphasized that the ideation process begins with defining basic guidelines, analyzing current reality, and then condensing the concept into concise statements and key pillars of the game.

The team has significantly changed its production methodology, abandoning rigid, long-term planning spanning years and the siloed work of individual departments. Instead of the classic waterfall approach, the developers use flexible iterations with planning at the level of short sprints and milestones, combining this with a long-term strategic task map. Work within the studio is now organized around interdisciplinary teams focused on creating a cohesive gaming experience, including specialists in gameplay, scriptwriting, sound, and environment design.

Over the past year, the North American team in Boston has doubled in size, bringing together veterans of the European office with new industry professionals. The studio's management emphasizes regular internal synchronization, open discussion of unconventional ideas, and a willingness to rework or cut content elements if they don't meet the overall quality standard. The team's primary goal in developing Cyberpunk 2 is to create a bold and profound work that seamlessly blends entertaining mechanics and a cinematic story without obvious black-and-white distinctions.

items.title: Cyberpunk 2077’s most expensive boss fight took two years to build and was redone four times
Cyberpunk 2077 Quest Director Admits DLC Success Won't Erase Disastrous Launch, But Is Proud of Phantom Liberty
items.summary: Now developers realize the importance of the game's technical state.
items.content:
0 27 September 2026, 05:44 Boris Piletskiy Now developers realize the importance of the game's technical state.

In September, CD Projekt RED developers and fans celebrated the anniversary of the Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty expansion. The game's quest director, Paweł Sasko, also joined the celebration.

The release version of Cyberpunk 2077 was full of various problems. Paweł Sasko said that one of the main lessons learned from the game's development history was understanding the importance of the game's technical state. It needs to be given as much attention as characters, world, and story, as bugs can prevent players from seeing the developers' original vision:

The development of Phantom Liberty ran in parallel with the massive changes that eventually made it into update 2.0. During this period, perks, cybernetic implants, the police system, car combat, artificial intelligence, the loot system, and many other mechanics were reworked. One lesson I learned from the entire Cyberpunk 2077 journey: the technical state needs to be given as much attention as characters, quests, and world-building. You can create something you genuinely believe in from a creative standpoint, but technical issues can prevent players from seeing it exactly as you intended. Image source: CD Projekt RED The Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty expansion received many positive reviews, but, according to Paweł Sasko, this DLC does not negate the fact that the original game's launch was problematic:

I think that Phantom Liberty doesn't erase that launch of Cyberpunk 2077, and speaking about the studio's history, I wouldn't want to ignore that episode. When Gabe Amatangelo and I went on stage at The Game Awards in 2023 to accept the award for Best Evolving Game, I thought of all the developers who continued to pour their hearts into Cyberpunk, and all of you who stayed with us, returned to the game, or decided to give it another chance. Paweł noted that working on the DLC he gained valuable skills:

[...] what I remember most is what working on this expansion taught me about leading game development, trusting people, giving decisions significance, giving characters space to unfold, and accepting the 'scars' that remain after creating such a complex project. .horizontal-20-1-b{width:100%;max-width:100%;min-height:300px;max-height:300px}@media (min-width:780px){.horizontal-20-1-b{width:100%;max-width:100%;min-height:160px;max-height:160px}} Currently, CD Projekt RED is working on the Cyberpunk 2 sequel, but the project has no specific release date or window.

The nearest release in CDPR's plans is The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered — the updated version of the game is expected to be released on September 29. Next year, the release of the story expansion Songs of the Past is expected, and The Witcher 4 is planned for launch in 2028.

items.title: Cyberpunk 2 leads say the sequel’s development is more collaborative after Cyberpunk 77’s “totally siloed” structure botched its launch release
items.summary: CD Projekt Red explains that Cyberpunk 2 is being made with a collaborative workforce after Cyberpunk 2077 suffered from siloed teams.
items.content:
Games Blog News Features Guides Evergreen guides for popular games, written by our in-house experts. FAQs Tutorials Cyberpunk 2 leads say the sequel’s development is more collaborative after Cyberpunk 77’s “totally siloed” structure botched its launch release Published:

CD Projekt’s Boston studio is currently hard at work on Cyberpunk 2 with over 150 developers working on the upcoming sequel . Developed on Unreal Engine 5, as the studio leaves its iconic REDEngine behind , the sequel is being crafted with a new team, on a new engine, with new ideas.

In a new interview , Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzynski and game director Gabriel Amatangelo explained that the sequel is being built in a more collaborative nature than its predecessor, learning from the failures of Cyberpunk 2077’s development.

In the interview, Sarzynski explained that the new studio in Boston is picking up from the improvements made during Phantom Liberty’s development. “We just completely switched our method,” he said.

“You don’t work really in disciplines. You work only in player-oriented pods which create player experiences. But to create player experiences, you need a little bit of everyone. You need someone from art, from audio, from gameplay, from narrative. And they always go totally hand-in-and talking to each other all the time. And that’s like an enormous change. And I think it served us really well on Phantom Liberty, and we would like to stick to it.”

Cyberpunk 2077’s launch development followed similar issues to other major games like Bethesda’s Starfield where there were a lot of developers siloed away from everyone else. “Overall, constant communication is just like the absolute life system of game development,” Sarzynski said. “Without it, everything falls apart immediately, especially with a project of our complexity.”

Amatangelo explained that not every developer is working in these player pods, adding that the team has a “hybrid approach” when needed. However, the game is being developed with a more collaborative mindset from the beginning, allowing more people to spot issues and provide feedback without getting lost in email chains.

Associate game director Pawel Sasko, who was the quest director for the first game, explained that the prior development structure of Cyberpunk 2077 was not effective. “In Cyberpunk, we’d been totally siloed, right?” he said. “The teams were working in waterfalls, in their bubbles. Like, art here and narrative here. And making all those people work together, communicate more… it qas a difficult process for our people internally here.”

Amatangelo recalls that this process was integral to the final outcome of Phantom Liberty, the only expansion for Cyberpunk 2077. “It’s like, beat up the ideas, you’re not beating up the person, you’re beating up the idea,” he said as he recalled wanting more people to deconstruct and improve his ideas for the expansion. “And that is the process of what you need to do. And everyone needs to feel comfortable with it or try to.”

Cyberpunk 2 is still years away with the game’s team size currently around a third of the size of The Witcher 4 ’s ongoing development. Right now, it’s unsure when the game will release or what platforms the game will release on, but the game is in active development at the time of writing.

Lewis White is a veteran games journalist with over a decade in the field. Starting with beloved Xbox website ICXM/XboxMAD, Lewis became the Gaming Editor at MSPoweruser before becoming the Editor in Chief of StealthOptional and Gfinityesports. Lewis later jumped to By Gamers For Gamers where he jumped to become EIC of VideoGamer and the host of the New VideoGamer Podcast prior to the website’s acquisition.

Over the years, Lewis has also seen long-form investigative pieces published in outlets such as Eurogamer, PCGamesN, Wireframe, Retro Gamer, Nintendo Life, and EDGE. Now, as the Editor in Chief of FRVR Blog, Lewis strives to bring the same level of quality journalism with interview-led content to the site in both written and audio form with the FRVR Podcast.

With a First Degree BA Hons in Games Journalism and Public Relations, Lewis has been a stable part of the British games press for over a decade, and has frequently displayed his love of Halo, The Elder Scrolls, Fallout, and other games pretty much everywhere he’s worked. And FRVR is no different.

items.title: DLSS 5 crosses the uncanny valley — and what's on the other side is worse
items.summary: Games now look too perfect, and now they look worse
items.content:
By Samarveer Singh Published Sep 25, 2026, 7:00 AM EDT Gaming has been Samarveer’s greatest passion, and the Literature graduate in him takes immense joy in dissecting games for their themes, messages, and impact. Samarveer holds a deep appreciation of gaming, and considers the platform to be the most immersive and impactful across all media. He can be found engaging with gaming communities online, always ready to debate the finer points of ray tracing or itching to write an 8-page collegiate thesis on any game that impacts him emotionally. Sign in to your XDA account Add Us Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread 6 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Much like any gamer in the world before me, and many after, I, too, have spent years desiring and chasing better graphics. I've obsessed over DLSS modes, ray tracing, frame rates, textures, lighting, and all the other little things that make a game look "closer to reality." As such, it feels rather strange to say this, but DLSS 5 has genuinely made me question whether that pursuit has finally gone too far.

From a technical standpoint, DLSS 5 is undeniably impressive . It makes the faces of characters sharper, enriches skin textures, and dramatizes lighting, too. Admittedly, the screenshots look ridiculously impressive, but the more I stare at them, the less convinced I am that I'm looking at "better graphics." Somewhere between photorealism and artificial perfection, something has gone missing. And I think I've finally figured out what it is.

Silicon alone can only do so much without software bearing the load

Close window.arrayOfGalleries["article-gallery-1-1241588057"] = '" Close "'; For most of my life, better game graphics have always meant something tangible. They translated to more polygons, better textures, smarter lighting , improved animation, and better materials. Every new generation has given artists new tools for making their worlds more convincing. Games like Death Stranding 2 , Cyberpunk 2077 , Alan Wake 2 , Kingdom Come: Deliverance II , and The Last of Us Part II Remastered are proof that this approach has taken us remarkably far. I can just look at a character in these games and know that I'm looking at an extremely photorealistic person without needing every pore sharpened out of existence.

Realism was never really about copying reality, nor should it have been. Instead, it's much more about coherence — where skin, eyes, hair, lighting, animation, and environments all had to agree with one another. We've talked about the uncanny valley for years now as the point where things didn't quite seem right, treating it like a ditch standing between games and photorealism.

The uncanny valley was warning us all along that we didn't need to make illusion stronger.

Astoundingly, DLSS 5 should make us all understand that the uncanny valley was a warning all along — a warning that adding more detail wouldn't necessarily make the illusion stronger. DLSS 5 changes that equation because previous versions of DLSS were fundamentally reconstruction technologies . They were trying to approximate imagery the renderer was already working toward.

Neural rendering, on the other hand, introduces something entirely different in the form of an AI model that can contribute to the final appearance itself. It synthesizes visual characteristics that weren't explicitly rendered by the game in the first place.

Never thought I'd say this, but if it's got path tracing, I want it on.

It's important to understand that DLSS 5 isn't just another jump in image quality. We aren't asking the renderer to execute an artist's vision with greater fidelity anymore. In asking a learned model to interpret what that vision should look like, the question thus becomes whether crossing the uncanny valley should have been the goal of game graphics in the first place.

Credit: @stopmrdomino.bsky.social Credit: Nvidia Credit: Nvidia Close Credit: @stopmrdomino.bsky.social Credit: Nvidia Credit: Nvidia window.arrayOfGalleries["article-gallery-2-2049132283"] = '" Credit: @stopmrdomino.bsky.social Credit: Nvidia Credit: Nvidia Close Credit: @stopmrdomino.bsky.social Credit: Nvidia Credit: Nvidia "'; I use DLSS 5 on my RTX 4070 Ti-powered PC with the right mods , but the more I use it, the stranger it gets. Nvidia's Neural Rendering layer gives characters more pores and sharper facial detail, and there's no denying the improvement in lighting. And yet, I often find myself staring at a face that looks like it has been run through an extremely expensive beauty filter. Everything is technically richer, but it's all the graphical equivalent of someone discovering Photoshop and immediately going hard on the clarity slider.

Officially, DLSS 5 is exclusive to Blackwell-era RTX 50-series GPUs. However, Nvidia has promised that the neural rendering layer of DLSS will come to RTX 40-series in due time.

With DLSS 5, there are no obvious artifacts to speak of, which is what makes it all harder to dismiss. When DLSS 5 works, it looks remarkably clean. But realism isn't a checklist where enough pores, wrinkles, and skin highlights eventually unlock "human." Real faces are messy , asymmetrical , and above all, inconsistent . These imperfections make faces recognizable in the first place — they aren't waiting around for AI to restore some missing detail.

That's where I think we've stumbled into a second uncanny valley. The first made characters look almost human. The second one, with DLSS 5, makes them look almost AI-human: polished, hyper-detailed and strangely uniform. Different games can start drifting toward the same visual idea of what a perfect face should look like, regardless of the artistic identity that made those characters distinct.

items.content:
To survive in Night City, you need someone to watch your back. On the way to the major leagues, V managed to gather a remarkable crew. You could even say, a crew to remember!

From trusted allies to unforgettable personalities, these are the people who helped shape V’s journey through the City of Dreams. This episode of It’s All About You is dedicated to the legendary crew that stood by V through every high and low.

Thank you for staying with us and expressing your love for Cyberpunk 2077 in the most creative ways possible. Don’t forget to check out our gallery to see more works, and, of course, share your creations with us: http://cdpred.ly/AAY

See you in the next episode!

items.content:
Listen up, Samurai! 🤘🔥

Celebrate five years of Cyberpunk 2077 in this special anniversary episode of It’s All About You, looking back on Night City’s unforgettable stories through the legends and music you met along your journey!

Sure, the city’s full of noise — sirens, synths, gunfire in the distance — but if there’s one song that became its soul, it’s “Never Fade Away.”

We brought together legendary artists from across the city of dreams to reinterpret this iconic track — each in their own voice, their own style, their own rebellion. ❤️‍🔥

Plug in, turn it up, and dive into our latest It’s All About You episode.

Because legends don’t fade.

items.title: Patch 2.31
items.summary: Patch 2.31 for Cyberpunk 2077 is now live! This update includes an AutoDrive upgrade and Photo Mode adjustments. It also addresses common issues encountered by players. For details, check the full list of changes below: Vehicles Updated Aut
items.content:
Patch 2.31 for Cyberpunk 2077 is now live!

This update includes an AutoDrive upgrade and Photo Mode adjustments. It also addresses common issues encountered by players. For details, check the full list of changes below:

Vehicles

  • Updated AutoDrive. When driving to a selected point, the vehicle now drives smoothly, overtakes blocking vehicles and no longer stops at traffic lights. Free Roam mode has also been upgraded to follow traffic rules and navigate the city more reliably.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where Johnny always spawned in the passenger seat when using the Delamain Cab service.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where applying CrystalCoat to the Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru caused its wheels to flash in different colors.

    [/*]

Photo Mode

  • Most of the new poses introduced in Update 2.3 now work with any gender.

    [/*]

  • Disabled NPC collision, which will make it easier to position NPCs on top of other objects with collision (e.g. on car hoods).

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where some of the poses didn't work for Royce.

    [/*]

Quests & Open World

  • Freedom - Fixed the journal entry that appears when the player chooses not to steal the Rayfield Caliburn "Mordred."

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Fixed an issue where, after V fails to pursue and stop Semimaru and receives a text from River saying he'll contact V soon, the follow-up message never arrives.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Fixed an issue where the Yaiba Semimaru could flip over during the chase, preventing the player from entering it.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - It's no longer possible to trigger the quest if River died during The Hunt.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Players can now acquire the Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru through AUTOFIXER even if they failed The Hunt, which normally unlocks the side quest where the vehicle is obtained.

    [/*]

  • Nitro (Youth Energy) - Fixed a game crash that could occur in certain circumstances after leaving the Yaiba showroom event.

    [/*]

  • Nitro (Youth Energy) - Fixed an issue where the proxy interface UI in the Yaiba showroom is cut off when the "Larger HUD Elements" setting is enabled.

    [/*]

Miscellaneous

  • Fixed several localization and lipsync issues in various languages.

    [/*]

  • Added a toggle to disable vignette. It can be found in Settings → Graphics → Basic.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on PC and Mac where Ray-Traced Reflections might not display correctly when enabled under certain conditions.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several issues with displaying text messages from Delamain.

    [/*]

  • Various fixes for fluff vendors.

    [/*]

PC-specific

  • Fixed an issue where NVIDIA Reflex could be disabled while DLSS Frame Generation was enabled, causing the screen to turn pink.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where Path Tracing didn't activate properly in certain scenarios.

    [/*]

Mac-specific

  • Fixed an issue where changing graphics presets on Mac set Screen Space Reflections to a higher setting compared to the equivalent presets on PC.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue causing a permanent white screen when Frame Generation is enabled while entering the braindance in The Information.

    [/*]

  • Selecting "Defaults" in Video Settings no longer turns HDR Mode off.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where setting the MetalFX DRS Maximum Resolution above the value applied by the “For this Mac” preset could cause visual artifacts.

    [/*]

  • Fixed the inverted behavior of the "Mute Game in Background" toggle in Settings.

    [/*]

  • Removed the outdated "(Requires Game Restart)" disclaimer from the mouseover description of the "Disable Spatial Audio" setting.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on the App Store version that caused the game to become stuck on the “Press Space to continue” breaching screen.

    [/*]

  • Various stability and performance optimizations.

    [/*]

items.content:
Surviving the City of Dreams is tough, but a choom at your side can make all the difference.

In our latest It’s All About You episode, we’re celebrating all of our iconic duos living on the edge! Night City wouldn’t shine quite so bright without them. 

Thank you for staying with us and expressing your love for Cyberpunk: Edgerunners in the most creative ways possible. Don't forget to check out our gallery to see more works, and, of course, share your creations with us: http://cdpred.ly/AAY. See you in the next episode!

items.content:
Update 2.3 lands tomorrow!

Experience Night City in a whole new way — this patch introduces 4 new vehicles, the AutoDrive feature, self-driving Delamain cabs and more! It also contains updates for CrystalCoat™ and Photo Mode, as well as support for AMD FSR 3.1 Frame Generation, Intel XeSS 2.0 and HDR10+ Gaming, among others.

Update 2.3 also brings Cyberpunk 2077 to a whole new platform: Mac with Apple silicon! If you already own the game on Steam, you can play it on your compatible device. To find out whether your Mac can run Cyberpunk 2077, please check the official requirements.

Read the list of changes for more info:

Vehicles

  • Added 4 new vehicles, including several Side Jobs tied to acquiring them:

    • Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru

      Reward from a new side job (to unlock, complete The Hunt and The Beast In Me).

      An additional side job unlocks the CrystalCoat™ feature for it.

      [/*]

    • Rayfield Caliburn "Mordred"

      Reward from a new side job (to unlock, complete The Beast in Me: Badlands, The Beast in Me: Santo Domingo, Transmission, and Search and Destroy)."

      [/*]

    • Yaiba ASM-R250 Muramasa

      Reward from a new side job (to unlock, purchase 1 Yaiba vehicle, purchase at least 3 vehicles through AUTOFIXER, and complete Reported Crime: You Play with Fire...).

      If you fail the side job, the vehicle can later be purchased through AUTOFIXER.

      [/*]

    • Chevillon Legatus 450 Aquila

      Available for purchase on AUTOFIXER.

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • Introducing AutoDrive! This cutting-edge, autonomous driving feature will take you to your chosen destination (i.e. job objective or placed pin on the map). If you have no set destination, it will take you on a leisurely ride through the streets of Night City. Simply hop in any of your vehicles, make sure you're on a road, and hold G (PC) / Left Stick (consoles) to activate. This feature is disabled when you enter combat or when your vehicle is heavily damaged.

    [/*]

  • Implemented Cinematic Camera for AutoDrive. Hold Q (PC) / D-Pad Right (consoles) to activate. Sit back and enjoy cinematic views of Night City as you cruise toward your destination.

    [/*]

  • Self-driving Delamain cabs are now available on demand! Simply open the menu to call vehicles, then select "Delamain Cab" from the list to request a ride. This feature unlocks after completing the job Don't Lose Your Mind (regardless of outcome) and receiving a message from Delamain.

    [/*]

  • Rayfield's CrystalCoat™ is now available for vehicles from partner brands, including motorcycles. Additionally, the infamous hacker known as Cosmetic_Troll exploited a vulnerability and created a cracked version of Rayfield's CrystalCoat™ technology for lower-end vehicles. Please note, however, that some models do not support the technology, such as heavily modded nomad vehicles and job-related vehicles.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where unique color schemes did not work properly on the Mizutani Shion MZ1 and MZ2.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where unique color scheme could not be applied properly to the Villefort Deleon "Vindicator".

    [/*]

Photo Mode

  • Added 27 new NPCs that can be spawned in Photo Mode, including Rita Wheeler, the Cassel twins, fixers, Dum Dum, the iguana, Brendan, and more.

    [/*]

  • You can now switch between alternative outfits for NPCs spawned in Photo Mode.

    [/*]

  • You can now switch between V's saved Wardrobe outfits in Photo Mode.

    [/*]

  • Added a confirmation pop-up when exiting Photo Mode to prevent accidental exits after setting up the perfect shot.

    [/*]

  • Added more customization options to the Look-At Camera feature, including an option for only the character's eyes to turn toward the camera instead of their entire body.

    [/*]

  • Added improvements to Lighting:

    • Lights now spawn around the camera instead of the player character.

      [/*]

    • Added an outline to the spotlight mesh and an indicator when it's off screen for better visibility.

      [/*]

    • Improved light movement speed on controllers.

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • Added multiple new stickers and frames, including iconic quotes and stylish overlays that let you turn your screenshots into Night City postcards – perfect for sharing memories from the City of Dreams.

    [/*]

  • Improved Depth of Field and moved it to the Camera tab.

    [/*]

  • Added a new Color Balance tab, allowing you to create your own custom filters.

    [/*]

  • Added a new Time and Weather tab:

    • Weather: includes rain, acid rain, fog, sandstorm, pollution, and sunny.

      [/*]

    • Time of Day: changes the time of day within Photo Mode.

      [/*]

    • Frame Forward: advances through an unlimited amount of frames to capture the perfect shot.

      [/*]

    • Game Speed: allows in-game time to progress while in Photo Mode."

      [/*]
    [/*]

Quality of Life & Accessibility

  • The game will now detect if the player is using inverted mouse button settings and automatically adjusts in-game button prompts accordingly.

    [/*]

  • Added an option to toggle aiming down sights in Settings → Controls.

    [/*]

Jobs & Open World

  • Cyberpsycho Sighting: Bloody Ritual - the "Crack the ritualist's shard" objective now properly disappears from the Journal after completing the objective.

    [/*]

  • Sex on Wheels - now properly appears in the Journal after receiving the message from Jake Estevez.

    [/*]

  • Shot by Both Sides - fixed an issue where selecting a specific dialogue option in the conversation with Bree created a nameless, iconless item in the player's Inventory.

    [/*]

  • Shot by Both Sides - fixed an issue where the button to go to the lower level didn't appear on the elevator panel.

    [/*]

Gameplay

  • Fixed an issue where, when using a controller in Trauma Drama, the controllable character would default to shooting upwards instead of forward.

    [/*]

  • Players can now drop more Cyberware Capacity Shards if some within the intended drop limit were previously missed.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue causing automatic weapons to fire slower than intended.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where the Official BARGHEST Tac Vest didn't drop from the scripted Airdrop as intended.

    [/*]

  • The level 60 Engineer perk no longer activates the EMP blast outside of combat or after entering a vehicle.

    [/*]

  • Added an option to replay the gameplay tutorial at any time via Settings → Controls.

    [/*]

Miscellaneous

  • Added an option to tell Johnny to go away after you look at him for a short while when he appears in the passenger seat. He takes the hint and disappears as a passenger for a couple days.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where the sound of V's Radioport could be randomly interrupted by the Radioports of nearby NPCs.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where History by Gazelle Twin and Trash Generation played too loudly compared to other songs on the radio.

    [/*]

  • Improved the HDR Setting screen: fixed the HDR calibration preview so it correctly reflects the chosen settings, and clarified the description of the "Tone-Mapping Midpoint" setting.

    [/*]

  • Updated the End User Licence Agreement. You will be asked to accept it again when you load the game after updating.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several visual issues with missing, clipping, or floating textures.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several localization issues in various languages.

    [/*]

PC-specific

  • Added support for AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 4 for compatible AMD GPUs. IMPORTANT: The FSR 4 option will not be available in the in-game settings until the supporting AMD driver is installed. Please note that the driver will be released at a later date.

    [/*]

  • Added support for AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution Frame Generation 3.1 for compatible hardware. It can now be used in combination with any upscaler.

    [/*]

  • Added support for ​Intel XeSS 2.0, with XeSS Frame Generation available on compatible hardware.

    [/*]

  • Added support for HDR10+ GAMING certified Intel GPUs. To enable this feature, your display must support the technology (find my display) and have "Game Mode" enabled. The HDR10+ GAMING toggle can be found in Settings in the Video tab.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where the DLSS Super Resolution Preset would invisibly revert from the CNN model to the Transformer model after restarting the game, even though the UI still displayed the CNN model as active.

    [/*]

  • Added more detailed information to the DLSS Super Resolution Preset tooltip in Settings to help players choose the best option for their setup.

    [/*]

  • Added the ability to move the mouse cursor to a different display while in Windowed Borderless mode.

    [/*]

  • Increased the maximum save size from 12 MB to 15 MB.

    [/*]

  • It will now be possible to rebind the key used to jump out of vehicles with the Stuntjock perk.

    [/*]
